rules.quote: Requirement terms: shall = mandatory and testable; should = recommended; may = optional.
rules.statement: Requirements marked 'shall' are mandatory and must be testable.

rules.quote: The IP transfers a stream of data words from a write clock domain to a read clock domain.
rules.statement: The FIFO must transfer a stream of data words from the write clock domain to the read clock domain.

rules.quote: Words are read in the order in which they were written.
rules.statement: Words must be read in the same order in which they were written (first-in first-out).

rules.quote: The two clocks may have different frequencies, but they are synchronous to each other: both derive from one source and keep a fixed phase relationship, for example 150 MHz and 100 MHz taken from one PLL (DEC-005).
rules.statement: The write and read clocks may have different frequencies, provided they are synchronous with a fixed phase relationship from one source.

rules.quote: Because the clocks are synchronous, the pointers cross from one domain to the other without synchronizers, as ordinary timed paths that static timing analysis (STA) closes.
rules.statement: Pointers must cross between clock domains without synchronizers, as ordinary timed paths closed by STA.

rules.quote: The special case of two equal clocks (one clock) is a normal use.
rules.statement: The write and read clocks may be equal (single clock) as a normal use case.

rules.quote: The interface and the options are inherited from the sibling IP 001_AsyncGrayFIFO (DEC-002), without its clock-domain-crossing logic: write and read requests with full and empty flags, threshold flags, overflow and underflow pulses, a show-ahead read, a hardware reset per domain, and a software reset with a handshake.
rules.statement: The FIFO must provide write and read requests, full and empty flags, threshold flags, overflow and underflow pulses, show-ahead read, a hardware reset per domain and a software reset with handshake.

rules.quote: Structural top m_vlsit_sfifo_top that instantiates the write module, the read module and the FIFO array module.
rules.statement: Structural top m_vlsit_sfifo_top must instantiate the write module, the read module and the FIFO array module.

rules.quote: Write module (write clock domain): write pointer, full and full-threshold flags, overflow pulse, memory write port, software reset FSM for the write side.
rules.statement: The write module in the write clock domain must contain write pointer, full and full-threshold flags, overflow pulse, memory write port and write-side software reset FSM.

rules.quote: Read module (read clock domain): read pointer, empty and empty-threshold flags, underflow pulse, memory read address, software reset FSM for the read side.
rules.statement: The read module in the read clock domain must contain read pointer, empty and empty-threshold flags, underflow pulse, memory read address and read-side software reset FSM.

rules.quote: FIFO array module: a pure RTL array, or a library SRAM with one write port and one read port (replacement branch).
rules.statement: The FIFO array module must be a pure RTL array or a library SRAM with one write port and one read port.

rules.quote: Any depth of 2 or more (not only a power of two), any data width of 1 bit or more. Feature ID: FEAT-001; Feature: FIFO storage for any depth of 2 or more and any data width; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-001, REQ-FUNC-002, REQ-FUNC-003, REQ-FUNC-006
rules.statement: The FIFO must support any depth of 2 or more, not only powers of two, and any data width of 1 bit or more.

rules.quote: One parameter that selects a direct pointer path or one retiming flop in the destination domain (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME). Feature ID: FEAT-007; Feature: Pointer retiming option; Required / optional: Optional; Configuration condition: PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1; Requirements: REQ-CLK-003, REQ-PERF-003, REQ-PERF-004
rules.statement: PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME must select either a direct pointer path or one retiming flop in the destination domain.

rules.quote: Gap-free streaming: with continuous write and continuous read there is only the initial latency and no gap (REQ-PERF-002). Feature ID: FEAT-008; Feature: Gap-free streaming; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Depth at least 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME; Requirements: REQ-PERF-001, REQ-PERF-002
rules.condition: depth at least 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME, continuous write and continuous read
rules.statement: Streaming must be gap-free, with only the initial latency and no gap.

rules.quote: Software reset with a four-phase handshake between the two domains. Feature ID: FEAT-009; Feature: Software reset with handshake; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-SRST-001 to REQ-SRST-008
rules.statement: Software reset must use a four-phase handshake between the two domains.

rules.quote: Item: Technology / library assumptions; Specification: Standard-cell library; optional SRAM macro with one write port and one read port behind a wrapper Feature ID: FEAT-010; Feature: SRAM macro replacement of the array; Required / optional: Optional; Configuration condition: PARA_SFIFO_MEM_USE_MACRO = 1; Requirements: REQ-RTL-002
rules.statement: The array may be replaced by an SRAM macro with one write port and one read port behind a wrapper.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-002; Feature: Two synchronous clocks of different frequencies, no synchronizer; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-CLK-001, REQ-CLK-002
rules.statement: The FIFO must support two synchronous clocks of different frequencies without a synchronizer.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-003; Feature: Full and empty flags with exact boundaries; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-004, REQ-FUNC-005, REQ-PERF-005
rules.statement: Full and empty flags must have exact boundaries.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-004; Feature: Full and empty threshold flags with static thresholds; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-007
rules.statement: Full and empty threshold flags must use static thresholds.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-005; Feature: Overflow and underflow pulses; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-008, REQ-FUNC-009
rules.statement: The FIFO must provide overflow and underflow pulses.

rules.quote: Feature ID: FEAT-006; Feature: Show-ahead read; Required / optional: Required; Configuration condition: Always present; Requirements: REQ-FUNC-002, REQ-IF-003
rules.statement: The FIFO must provide show-ahead read.

rules.quote: Ref ID: REF-003; Document and revision: VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2, VLSIT_RTL_Generator_AI_Model\spec_template\VLSIT_RTL_Design_Rule.md; Applicable clauses: All applicable rules; Authority / notes: Mandatory RTL coding, hierarchy, reset, CDC and naming baseline REF-003 is the mandatory RTL coding, hierarchy, reset, CDC and naming baseline.
rules.statement: The RTL must follow VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2 (REF-003) as the mandatory coding, hierarchy, reset, CDC and naming baseline.

rules.quote: REF-001 explains the inherited behavior; it never overrides this specification.
rules.statement: REF-001 (the sibling AsyncGrayFIFO specification) must not override this specification; where they differ, this specification prevails.

rules.quote: A conflict is resolved by revising the requirement or choosing a compliant implementation, not by a local RTL exception.
rules.condition: When a conflict arises between requirements
rules.statement: Conflicts must be resolved by revising the requirement or choosing a compliant implementation, not by a local RTL exception.

rules.statement: A blocked read shall not raise o_underflow.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-SRST-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The read side shall reset its pointer first and acknowledge; the write side shall then reset its pointer; the read side shall be released first and the write side last. rules.statement: Read side shall reset its pointer first and acknowledge, then write side resets its pointer; read side is released first, write side last.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-SRST-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The read side shall reset its pointer first and acknowledge; the write side shall then reset its pointer; the read side shall be released first and the write side last. The handshake shall be four-phase.; Source: DEC-007, REF-001; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009; waveform WF-013
rules.statement: The software reset handshake shall be four-phase.

rules.statement: The FIFO shall be empty, both pointers 0, and every stored word discarded.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-SRST-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: At the end of a software reset sequence the FIFO shall be empty, both pointers shall be 0, and every stored word shall be discarded. The memory content shall not be erased.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009
rules.statement: The memory content shall not be erased.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-SRST-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_sw_rst_busy shall be the output of a flip-flop. rules.quote: ID: REQ-SRST-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_sw_rst_busy shall be the output of a flip-flop. rules.statement: The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1.

rules.statement: A hardware reset shall have priority over a software reset and bring both FSMs to RUN.

rules.statement: The IP shall accept the parameter values listed in Section 8.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall accept one write per write-clock cycle and one read per read-clock cycle.; Source: DEC-012; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-007; waveform WF-008
rules.statement: The IP shall accept one write per write-clock cycle and one read per read-clock cycle.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: With i_wr_en and i_rd_en held at 1, there shall be only the initial latency and no gap: after the first word is available, every read-clock cycle in which the writer is not the limit accepts a read, and every write-clock cycle in which the reader is not the limit accepts a write. rules.condition: i_wr_en and i_rd_en held at 1, depth >= 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME
rules.statement: There shall be only initial latency and no gap: every cycle where the other side is not limiting accepts a read or write.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: After a write into an empty FIFO, o_empty shall fall after the first rising edge of i_clk_rd that is strictly later than the write edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0), or after the second such edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1). o_rd_data shall show the new word at that moment.; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; waveform WF-001, WF-006, WF-007

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: After a read from a full FIFO, o_full shall fall after the first rising edge of i_clk_wr that is strictly later than the read edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0), or after the second such edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1).; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; waveform WF-006, WF-007
rules.statement: o_full shall fall after the first strictly later i_clk_wr rising edge (RETIME 0) or the second (RETIME 1).

rules.quote: ID: REQ-PERF-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: The boundary flags shall be exact in their own domain with no extra latency: o_full shall be 1 in the cycle after the write that stores the last free place, and o_empty shall be 1 in the cycle after the read that takes the last word.; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-003, TEST-004
rules.statement: o_full shall be 1 the cycle after the write storing the last free place; o_empty shall be 1 the cycle after the read taking the last word.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-RTL-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and shall use the hierarchy of Section 14.2.; Source: REF-003; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Lint and rule check: TEST-014
rules.statement: The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and use the hierarchy of Section 14.2.

rules.statement: The library SRAM shall be instantiated only inside the VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R wrapper in 000_Common, with instance name u_dont_touch_ plus function name, behaving like the array branch.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-RTL-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall contain no synchronizer module and no cell wrapper other than the SRAM wrapper. rules.statement: The IP shall contain no synchronizer module and no cell wrapper other than the SRAM wrapper; the retiming flop shall be a plain RTL flip-flop.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-VER-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: Every waveform of the waveform plan (Section 10.3) shall exist as an image with its WaveJSON source, and the prototype scripts shall reproduce them.; Source: DEC-011; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: File check and rerun: TEST-016
rules.statement: Every waveform of the plan shall exist as an image with WaveJSON source, reproducible by prototype scripts.

rules.quote: ID: REQ-VER-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The scoreboard regression shall cover the depths 2, 3, 5, 8 and 12, both values of PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME, and several clock ratios including equal clocks, and shall report no error.; Source: DEC-005; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Regression: TEST-017
rules.statement: Scoreboard regression shall cover depths 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, both PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME values and several clock ratios including equal, with no error.

rules.statement: FEAT-007 and FEAT-010 must be selected by a parameter at elaboration and be present or absent, not run-time disabled.

rules.quote: The port list is the same in every configuration except for widths.
rules.statement: The port list must be identical in every configuration except for port widths.

rules.quote: Illegal combinations are listed in Section 8.
rules.statement: Parameter combinations listed as illegal in Section 8 must not be used.

rules.quote: The flags are flip-flops computed from the next pointer values (look-ahead), so each flag is exact at the edge of its own domain and conservative only by the visibility of the other side (DEC-013).
rules.statement: Flags are flip-flops computed from the next pointer values (look-ahead), so each flag is exact at its own domain's clock edge and conservative only by the other side's pointer visibility.

rules.quote: Block: m_vlsit_sfifo_wr; Responsibility: Write pointer, write acceptance, full and full-threshold flags, overflow pulse, memory write port, retiming flops of the read pointer and the acknowledge, software reset FSM of the write side with its request and busy flops; Inputs / outputs: Write interface, read pointer and acknowledge from the read side, write pointer and request to the read side, memory write port; Clock/reset domain: CLK-WR / RST-WR; State or storage: Write pointer, flag flops, FSM state, request, busy, optional retiming flops
rules.statement: m_vlsit_sfifo_wr owns the write pointer, write acceptance, full and full-threshold flags, overflow pulse, memory write port and write-side software reset FSM, in CLK-WR/RST-WR domain.

rules.quote: Block: m_vlsit_sfifo_rd; Responsibility: Read pointer, read acceptance, empty and empty-threshold flags, underflow pulse, memory read address (address of the next read pointer), retiming flops of the write pointer and the request, software reset FSM of the read side with its acknowledge flop; Inputs / outputs: Read interface, write pointer and request from the write side, read pointer and acknowledge to the write side, memory read port; Clock/reset domain: CLK-RD / RST-RD; State or storage: Read pointer, flag flops, FSM state, acknowledge, optional retiming flops
rules.statement: m_vlsit_sfifo_rd owns the read pointer, read acceptance, empty and empty-threshold flags, underflow pulse, memory read address (next read pointer) and read-side reset FSM, in CLK-RD/RST-RD domain.

rules.quote: Block: m_vlsit_sfifo_top; Responsibility: Structural wrapper: interface, parameters, interconnect and the three instances; Inputs / outputs: All ports of Section 6.2; Clock/reset domain: CLK-WR, CLK-RD; State or storage: None
rules.statement: m_vlsit_sfifo_top is a structural wrapper holding interface, parameters, interconnect and the three instances, with no state or storage.

rules.quote: At a rising edge of i_clk_wr with i_wr_en = 1 and o_full = 0 (and no software reset block) the word is stored at the address of the write pointer, the write pointer increments, and the flags are recomputed for the next cycle.
rules.condition: At a rising edge of i_clk_wr with i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0 and no software reset block
rules.statement: The word on i_wr_data is stored at the write pointer address, the write pointer increments, and flags are recomputed for the next cycle.

rules.quote: The read side uses it at its next rising edge that is strictly later (directly, or one edge later through the retiming flop).
rules.statement: The read side uses the new write pointer at its next strictly later rising edge, directly or one edge later through the retiming flop.

rules.quote: The read flag register is loaded at that edge together with the memory output register, so the empty flag and the data change together.
rules.condition: When the read side uses the new write pointer
rules.statement: The read flag register and memory output register load at the same edge, so o_empty and the read data change together.

rules.quote: At a rising edge of i_clk_rd with i_rd_en = 1 and o_empty = 0 the word shown on o_rd_data is taken, the read pointer increments, and the memory output register already loads the following word (the memory read address is the address of the next read pointer). The memory read address always refers to the next read pointer, so the output register holds the word at the read pointer whenever o_empty is 0.
rules.condition: At a rising edge of i_clk_rd with i_rd_en = 1 and o_empty = 0
rules.statement: The word on o_rd_data is taken, the read pointer increments, and the output register loads the following word; the memory read address is the next read pointer's address.

rules.quote: The read pointer is visible to the write side at its next strictly later rising edge (directly, or one edge later), where o_full may fall.
rules.statement: The read pointer becomes visible to the write side at its next strictly later rising edge, directly or one edge later, where o_full may fall.

rules.quote: The occupancy (write pointer minus read pointer, modulo two times the depth) is between 0 and PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH.
rules.statement: Occupancy (write pointer minus read pointer modulo twice the depth) stays between 0 and PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH.

rules.quote: No write is accepted while o_full is 1, and no read is accepted while o_empty is 1.
rules.statement: No write is accepted while o_full is 1, and no read is accepted while o_empty is 1.

rules.quote: o_full is 1 whenever the occupancy is PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH; o_empty is 1 whenever the occupancy is 0.
rules.statement: o_full is 1 whenever occupancy is PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH, and o_empty is 1 whenever occupancy is 0.

rules.quote: The write side never sees a read pointer that is ahead of the real one, and the read side never sees a write pointer that is ahead of the real one: the views only lag.
rules.statement: The write side never sees a read pointer ahead of the real one, and the read side never sees a write pointer ahead of the real one; views only lag.

rules.quote: Pointers and flags change only at a rising edge of the clock of their own domain.
rules.statement: Pointers and flags change only at a rising edge of the clock of their own domain.

rules.quote: Interface ID: IF-001; Type and revision: Custom FIFO write interface (request, data, full and overflow flags, thresholds); Role: Slave of the writer; Direction at IP boundary: Requests in, status out; Clock domain: CLK-WR; Required / optional: Required; Configurations: All
rules.statement: IF-001 custom FIFO write interface is required in all configurations, acts as slave of the writer in CLK-WR with requests in and status out.

rules.quote: Interface ID: IF-002; Type and revision: Custom FIFO read interface (request, show-ahead data, empty and underflow flags, thresholds); Role: Slave of the reader; Direction at IP boundary: Requests in, data and status out; Clock domain: CLK-RD; Required / optional: Required; Configurations: All
rules.statement: IF-002 custom FIFO read interface is required in all configurations, acts as slave of the reader in CLK-RD with requests in and data and status out.

rules.quote: Interface ID: IF-003; Type and revision: Software reset (request level and busy output); Role: Slave of the controller; Direction at IP boundary: Request in, busy out; Clock domain: CLK-WR; Required / optional: Required; Configurations: All
rules.statement: IF-003 software reset interface is required in all configurations, slave of the controller in CLK-WR, with request input and busy output.

rules.quote: Interface ID: IF-004; Type and revision: Clocks and hardware resets; Role: Receiver; Direction at IP boundary: Inputs; Clock domain: CLK-WR, CLK-RD; Required / optional: Required; Configurations: All
rules.statement: IF-004 clocks and hardware resets are required inputs in all configurations, in domains CLK-WR and CLK-RD.

rules.quote: The top-level port list never depends on a parameter value except for widths (REF-003 PRT-03).
rules.statement: The top-level port list must not depend on any parameter value except for port widths.

rules.quote: Port: o_sw_rst_busy; Direction: Output; Width: 1; Meaning (function): Software reset busy: writes are possible again when it is 0; Clock domain: CLK-WR; Signal type: Level (flop output, active-high); Reset / idle value: 0; Timing / sampling: Changes at a rising edge of i_clk_wr; Configurations: All
rules.statement: o_sw_rst_busy is a flop output that changes only at a rising edge of i_clk_wr and is 0 when writes are possible again.

rules.quote: Type: Clock; Meaning: Free-running clock; What the user shall know: Rising edge active; no gating inside the IP
rules.statement: Clocks are rising-edge active, and the IP performs no clock gating inside.

rules.quote: Type: Reset; Meaning: Reset level; What the user shall know: A level, not a pulse. It stays low for at least one edge of its clock and is released synchronously outside the IP
rules.statement: A reset is a level that stays low for at least one edge of its clock and is released synchronously to that clock outside the IP.

rules.quote: Type: Level; Meaning: A signal that holds its value; What the user shall know: A request is sampled at every edge: each edge at which it is 1 and the acceptance condition holds is one transaction. A flag stays 1 for as long as its condition holds
rules.condition: A request is 1 at a clock edge and the acceptance condition holds
rules.statement: A Level request is sampled at every edge, and each such edge is one transaction; a flag stays 1 as long as its condition holds.

rules.quote: Type: Pulse; Meaning: One-cycle event; What the user shall know: Output of a flop, 1 for exactly one clock period after the edge that carried the event, returns to 0 by itself, not sticky
rules.statement: A Pulse output is a flop output that is 1 for exactly one clock period after the event edge, returns to 0 by itself and is not sticky.

rules.quote: Type: Data; Meaning: A bus with a qualifier; What the user shall know: Valid only while or when the qualifier named in the brackets is true
rules.statement: Data signals are valid only while or when their named qualifier is true, e.g. o_rd_data valid when o_empty = 0.

rules.quote: Type: Static; Meaning: A configuration value; What the user shall know: Not changed while the FIFO is in use; no clock domain
rules.condition: While the FIFO is in use
rules.statement: Static configuration values such as i_full_thr and i_empty_thr must not be changed while the FIFO is in use; they have no clock domain.

rules.quote: The write is accepted when i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0 and writes are not blocked by the software reset.
rules.condition: i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0 and writes not blocked by software reset
rules.statement: The write is accepted when i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0 and writes are not blocked by the software reset.

rules.quote: A request is never accepted while o_full = 1.
rules.statement: A write request is never accepted while o_full = 1.

rules.quote: The read is accepted when i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 0 and reads are not blocked. o_rd_data is the word to be taken and is valid for the whole cycle before the accepting edge.
rules.condition: i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 0 and reads not blocked
rules.statement: The read is accepted when i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 0 and reads are not blocked; o_rd_data is valid for the whole cycle before the accepting edge.

rules.quote: After an accepted read, o_rd_data shows the next word in the next cycle, with no bubble, if another word is visible.
rules.condition: After an accepted read, if another word is visible
rules.statement: o_rd_data shows the next word in the next cycle with no bubble.

rules.quote: A view may lag the real occupancy in the direction that is safe (full late to fall, empty late to fall), never in the unsafe direction.
rules.statement: A flag view may lag real occupancy only in the safe direction (full late to fall, empty late to fall), never in the unsafe direction.

rules.quote: A rejected write or read changes nothing but raises the one-cycle overflow or underflow pulse.
rules.condition: A write or read is rejected
rules.statement: A rejected write or read changes no state but raises the one-cycle overflow or underflow pulse.

rules.quote: Case: Write into a FIFO that is not full; Legal behavior: Word stored, write pointer increments; Illegal / unsupported case: None; IP response: Accepted at the edge; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-001
rules.condition: Write while FIFO is not full
rules.statement: A write into a FIFO that is not full is accepted at the edge, the word is stored and the write pointer increments.

rules.quote: Case: Write while o_full = 1; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Write into a full FIFO; IP response: Dropped, o_overflow pulse in the next cycle; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-004, REQ-FUNC-008
rules.statement: A write while o_full = 1 is dropped and an o_overflow pulse occurs in the next cycle.

rules.quote: Case: Read from a FIFO that is not empty; Legal behavior: Word taken, next word shown; Illegal / unsupported case: None; IP response: Accepted at the edge; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-002
rules.condition: Read while FIFO is not empty
rules.statement: A read from a non-empty FIFO is accepted at the edge, the word is taken and the next word is shown.

rules.quote: Case: Read while o_empty = 1; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Read of an empty FIFO; IP response: Dropped, o_underflow pulse in the next cycle; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-005, REQ-FUNC-009
rules.statement: A read while o_empty = 1 is dropped and an o_underflow pulse occurs in the next cycle.

rules.quote: Case: Write or read while the software reset blocks the side; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Request during the software reset; IP response: Dropped, no overflow or underflow pulse; Requirement IDs: REQ-SRST-002, REQ-SRST-003
rules.condition: Write or read while the software reset blocks that side
rules.statement: A request during software-reset blocking is dropped, with no o_overflow or o_underflow pulse.

rules.quote: Case: Request while a hardware reset is asserted; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Request during the reset; IP response: Not defined (the IP is in reset); Requirement IDs: REQ-RESET-002
rules.condition: Request while a hardware reset is asserted
rules.statement: IP response to a request during hardware reset is not defined.

rules.quote: Case: Threshold input changed while the FIFO is in use; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: i_full_thr or i_empty_thr not static; IP response: The flag may take a wrong value for some cycles; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-007
rules.condition: Threshold input changed while the FIFO is in use
rules.statement: If a threshold input is not static, the flag may take a wrong value for some cycles.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: Not applicable; From → to: Not applicable; Signals: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-23): the two clocks are synchronous, so there is no clock-domain crossing and no synchronizer (DEC-005, DEC-010). rules.condition: When constraints are declared for the IP
rules.statement: The two clocks i_clk_wr and i_clk_rd shall be declared as related clocks of one source.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: Not applicable; From → to: Not applicable; Signals: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-23): the two clocks are synchronous, so there is no clock-domain crossing and no synchronizer (DEC-005, DEC-010). The paths between the domains are timed paths: the write pointer and the request go from CLK-WR to CLK-RD, the read pointer and the acknowledge go from CLK-RD to CLK-WR; each starts at a flop and ends at a flop or at the flag logic (Section 17.1); Structure: Not applicable; Reset handling: Not applicable; Constraints / verification: The two clocks shall be declared as related clocks of one source, and no asynchronous clock group or false path shall be set between them (REQ-CLK-002, TEST-015)
rules.condition: When constraints are declared for the IP

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME; Purpose: Pointer path: 0 = direct, 1 = one retiming flop in the destination domain (DEC-006); Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 or 1; Dependencies / invalid combinations: None; Effect: Latency of the flags and timing of the crossing paths; the function is the same
rules.statement: PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME changes only flag latency and crossing path timing; the FIFO function is the same for both values.

rules.quote: Quantity: Pointer; Width: LPARA_PTR_W; Encoding / range: Unsigned, 0 to 2 x DEPTH - 1; after 2 x DEPTH - 1 it returns to 0; Extension / truncation: Increment is explicit; no truncation; Overflow / invalid behavior: The pointer never exceeds its range
rules.statement: The pointer must never exceed its range of 2 x DEPTH - 1; increment is explicit with no truncation.

rules.quote: Quantity: Occupancy; Width: LPARA_PTR_W + 1 (internal); Encoding / range: Write pointer minus read pointer: the difference if the write pointer is not below the read pointer, otherwise the difference plus 2 x DEPTH; Extension / truncation: Result is 0 to DEPTH; Overflow / invalid behavior: Cannot exceed DEPTH because the full flag blocks writes
rules.statement: Occupancy must not exceed DEPTH, because the full flag blocks writes.

rules.quote: Quantity: Threshold; Width: LPARA_OCC_W; Encoding / range: Unsigned occupancy value, 0 to DEPTH; Extension / truncation: Zero-extended for the comparison; Overflow / invalid behavior: A value above DEPTH makes o_full_thr never 1 and o_empty_thr always 1
rules.statement: The threshold, of width LPARA_OCC_W, is an unsigned occupancy value from 0 to DEPTH and is zero-extended for the comparison.

rules.quote: The data path has no mode: the flags alone decide acceptance.
rules.statement: The data path has no mode; acceptance of writes and reads is decided only by the flags.

rules.quote: Write reset FSM (m_vlsit_sfifo_wr, reg_fsm_srst_current_state, 3 bits; encodings 5 to 7 recover to RUN): Mode/state: ENUM_ST_RUN; Entry condition: Reset, or the end of REL; Behavior: Normal operation; Exit condition: i_rst_n_sw = 0: REQ; Outputs / side effects: o_sw_rst_busy 0, request 0 Mode/state: ENUM_ST_REQ; Entry condition: Request taken; Behavior: Writes blocked; request raised; wait for the acknowledge; Exit condition: Acknowledge seen: PTR; Outputs / side effects: o_sw_rst_busy 1, request 1
rules.condition: Write reset FSM in ENUM_ST_RUN and i_rst_n_sw = 0
rules.statement: Write reset FSM leaves RUN to REQ when i_rst_n_sw = 0, blocks writes, raises request and drives o_sw_rst_busy 1 until acknowledge is seen.

rules.quote: Write reset FSM (m_vlsit_sfifo_wr, reg_fsm_srst_current_state, 3 bits; encodings 5 to 7 recover to RUN):
rules.condition: Write reset FSM state encoding is 5 to 7
rules.statement: Write reset FSM state encodings 5 to 7 recover to RUN.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_PTR; Entry condition: Acknowledge seen; Behavior: The write pointer is reset to 0 (one cycle); Exit condition: Always: HOLD; Outputs / side effects: Request 1
rules.condition: Write reset FSM in ENUM_ST_PTR after acknowledge seen
rules.statement: In ENUM_ST_PTR the write pointer is reset to 0 for one cycle, request stays 1, and the FSM always moves to HOLD.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_HOLD; Entry condition: After PTR; Behavior: Wait for i_rst_n_sw = 1; Exit condition: i_rst_n_sw = 1: REL; Outputs / side effects: Request 1 Mode/state: ENUM_ST_REL; Entry condition: i_rst_n_sw is 1 again; Behavior: Request dropped; wait for the acknowledge to fall and the read pointer seen as 0 (flush check); Exit condition: Acknowledge 0 and read pointer 0: RUN; Outputs / side effects: Request 0, o_sw_rst_busy 1
rules.condition: Write reset FSM in HOLD or REL
rules.statement: HOLD waits with request 1 until i_rst_n_sw = 1, then REL drops request, keeps o_sw_rst_busy 1 and returns to RUN when acknowledge is 0 and read pointer is 0.

rules.quote: Read reset FSM (m_vlsit_sfifo_rd, reg_fsm_srst_current_state, 2 bits; encoding 3 recovers to RUN): Mode/state: ENUM_ST_RUN; Entry condition: Reset, or the end of ACK; Behavior: Normal operation; Exit condition: Request seen: RST; Outputs / side effects: Acknowledge 0
rules.condition: Read reset FSM encoding 3, or in RUN
rules.statement: Read reset FSM encoding 3 recovers to RUN; in RUN acknowledge is 0 and request seen moves it to RST.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_RST; Entry condition: Request seen; Behavior: Reads blocked; the read pointer is reset to 0 (one cycle); Exit condition: Always: ACK; Outputs / side effects: Acknowledge rises at the exit edge
rules.statement: In ENUM_ST_RST reads are blocked, the read pointer is reset to 0 for one cycle, the FSM goes to ACK and acknowledge rises at the exit edge.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_ACK; Entry condition: After RST; Behavior: Reads blocked; acknowledge held; Exit condition: Request 0 and write pointer seen as 0 (flush check): RUN; Outputs / side effects: Acknowledge 1
rules.statement: In ENUM_ST_ACK reads are blocked and acknowledge held at 1 until request is 0 and write pointer is seen as 0, then FSM returns to RUN.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-001; Inputs / preconditions: i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0, no software reset block; Processing semantics: Store i_wr_data at the write address, increment the write pointer; Result / completion: Word stored; o_empty falls in the read domain; o_full rises at once if it was the last free place; Latency / ordering: The read side sees it after the first (PTR_RETIME 0) or second (PTR_RETIME 1) later read edge

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-001; Inputs / preconditions: i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0, no software reset block; Processing semantics: Store i_wr_data at the write address, increment the write pointer; Result / completion: Word stored; o_empty falls in the read domain; o_full rises at once if it was the last free place; Latency / ordering: The read side sees it after the first (PTR_RETIME 0) or second (PTR_RETIME 1) later read edge Cycle / event: First read edge strictly after E_w (E_r1); Input condition: Any; State/action: The read side loads o_empty and the memory output register from the new write pointer (direct), or captures the write pointer in the retiming flop; Output condition: PTR_RETIME 0: o_empty falls and o_rd_data shows the new word after E_r1. rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-002; Inputs / preconditions: i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 0, no software reset block; Processing semantics: Take the word of o_rd_data, increment the read pointer, load the next word into the output register; Result / completion: Next word shown; o_empty rises at once if it was the last word; Latency / ordering: One word per read cycle; o_full falls in the write domain after the first or second later write edge Cycle / event: First write edge strictly after E_r (E_w1); Input condition: Any; State/action: The write side recomputes o_full from the new read pointer (direct), or captures the read pointer first; Output condition: PTR_RETIME 0: o_full falls after E_w1. rules.statement: o_full falls in the write domain after the first (PTR_RETIME 0) or second (PTR_RETIME 1) write edge strictly after the read edge.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-003; Inputs / preconditions: i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 1, no block; Processing semantics: Reject the write, change nothing; Result / completion: o_overflow pulse in the next cycle; Latency / ordering: None

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-004; Inputs / preconditions: i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 1, no block; Processing semantics: Reject the read, change nothing; Result / completion: o_underflow pulse in the next cycle; Latency / ordering: None
rules.statement: The read is rejected with no state change and o_underflow pulses in the next cycle.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-005; Inputs / preconditions: Static i_full_thr and i_empty_thr; Processing semantics: Compare the occupancy of the own view with the threshold; Result / completion: o_full_thr and o_empty_thr; Latency / ordering: Updated at every edge of the own clock
rules.statement: o_full_thr and o_empty_thr compare the occupancy of the own domain view with the thresholds and update at every edge of the own clock.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-006; Inputs / preconditions: i_rst_n_sw = 0; Processing semantics: Sequence of Section 10.7: block, reset read pointer, reset write pointer, release; Result / completion: FIFO empty, pointers 0, o_sw_rst_busy 0; Latency / ordering: A few cycles of the two clocks; see Section 10.7
rules.statement: Software reset runs the sequence block, reset read pointer, reset write pointer, release, ending with FIFO empty, pointers 0 and o_sw_rst_busy 0.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-007; Inputs / preconditions: i_rst_n_wr = 0 or i_rst_n_rd = 0; Processing semantics: Asynchronous clear of the state of the domain; Result / completion: FIFO empty, reset values of Section 7.3; Latency / ordering: Immediate
rules.statement: The state of the domain is cleared asynchronously and immediately, leaving the FIFO empty with reset values.

rules.statement: The writer never stalls; the faster reader waits through o_empty and o_underflow only because the writer is slower.

rules.statement: Pointer wraps over 0 to 9 and address over 0 to 4.

rules.quote: Active edge: the rising edge of the clock of the signal's own domain. Inputs are sampled at the edge that ends a cycle; flop outputs change after the edge that starts it.
rules.statement: The active edge is the rising edge of the signal's own domain clock; inputs are sampled at the edge ending a cycle and flop outputs change after the edge starting it.

rules.quote: The writer never stalls; the faster reader waits (o_empty, o_underflow) only because the writer is slower. o_rd_data is meaningful only while o_empty is 0 (source waveforms/sfifo_wf011_back_to_back_read_faster.json).*
rules.statement: o_rd_data is meaningful only while o_empty is 0.

rules.quote: WF-005: o_full_thr rises at occupancy 6 and o_empty_thr falls at occupancy 3 (thresholds 6 and 2, depth 8) (source waveforms/sfifo_wf005_thresholds.json).*
rules.statement: o_full_thr rises at occupancy 6 and o_empty_thr falls at occupancy 3.

rules.quote: WF-004: read requests on an empty FIFO give one o_underflow pulse each (source waveforms/sfifo_wf004_empty_underflow.json).*
rules.statement: Each read request on an empty FIFO gives one o_underflow pulse.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: Write edge E_w; Input condition: i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0; State/action: Word stored, write pointer increments, flags of the write domain recomputed; Output condition: o_full may rise in the next cycle (if it was the last place)
rules.statement: The word is stored, write pointer increments, write-domain flags are recomputed, and o_full may rise in the next cycle if it was the last place.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: First read edge strictly after E_w (E_r1); Input condition: Any; State/action: The read side loads o_empty and the memory output register from the new write pointer (direct), or captures the write pointer in the retiming flop; Output condition: PTR_RETIME 0: o_empty falls and o_rd_data shows the new word after E_r1. rules.condition: First read edge strictly after write edge
rules.statement: With PTR_RETIME 0, o_empty falls and o_rd_data shows the new word after E_r1; with PTR_RETIME 1, after E_r2.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: Read edge E_r; Input condition: i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 0; State/action: Word taken, read pointer increments, next word loaded; Output condition: o_empty rises in the next cycle if it was the last word
rules.statement: The word is taken, read pointer increments, next word loaded, and o_empty rises in the next cycle if it was the last word.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: First write edge strictly after E_r (E_w1); Input condition: Any; State/action: The write side recomputes o_full from the new read pointer (direct), or captures the read pointer first; Output condition: PTR_RETIME 0: o_full falls after E_w1. PTR_RETIME 1: after E_w2
rules.condition: First write edge strictly after read edge
rules.statement: With PTR_RETIME 0, o_full falls after E_w1; with PTR_RETIME 1, after E_w2.

rules.quote: When the two edges coincide (equal clocks, or an edge of the common least common multiple), the edge that coincides does not count as "strictly later": the pointer written at that edge is seen at the next edge. This is why WF-001 shows o_empty falling one full cycle after the write edge.
rules.condition: Source and destination clock edges coincide
rules.statement: A coinciding edge does not count as strictly later; the pointer written at that edge is seen at the next edge.

rules.quote: Simultaneous write and read are independent (different pointers); a write and a read at the same clock edge are both accepted when the flags allow.
rules.condition: a write and a read occur at the same clock edge and the flags allow both
rules.statement: Simultaneous write and read are independent and both are accepted at the same clock edge when o_full and o_empty allow.

rules.quote: One word per write-clock cycle and one word per read-clock cycle (REQ-PERF-001).
rules.statement: The FIFO accepts one word per write-clock cycle and delivers one word per read-clock cycle (REQ-PERF-001).

rules.quote: Event: Write edge to the fall of o_empty; PTR_RETIME = 0: 2 ns: the first read edge strictly after the write edge (WF-006); PTR_RETIME = 1: 10 ns, one read period (8 ns) more (WF-007)
rules.condition: after a write into an empty FIFO
rules.statement: o_empty falls at the first read edge strictly after the write edge when PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0, and one read period later when PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1.

rules.quote: Event: Equal clocks: first read accepted after the write edge; PTR_RETIME = 0: 2 cycles (WF-001); PTR_RETIME = 1: 3 cycles
rules.statement: The first read accepted after the write edge occurs after 2 cycles with PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0 and after 3 cycles with PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1.

rules.quote: Event: Read edge to the fall of o_full; PTR_RETIME = 0: First write edge strictly after the read edge; PTR_RETIME = 1: One write edge more
rules.condition: after a read from a full FIFO
rules.statement: o_full falls at the first write edge strictly after the read edge when PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0, and one write edge later when PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1.

rules.quote: Event: Last word read to o_empty = 1; PTR_RETIME = 0: Next cycle; PTR_RETIME = 1: Next cycle
rules.statement: o_empty = 1 in the next cycle after the last word is read, for both PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME values.

rules.quote: Event: Last free place written to o_full = 1; PTR_RETIME = 0: Next cycle; PTR_RETIME = 1: Next cycle
rules.condition: the last free place is written
rules.statement: o_full = 1 in the next cycle after the last free place is written, for both PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME values.

rules.quote: Gap-free streaming. With i_wr_en and i_rd_en held at 1 there is only the initial latency.
rules.statement: Streaming has no gaps beyond the initial latency.

rules.quote: The sweep waveforms/proto/run_regress.py (waveforms/sfifo_min_depth_table.txt) measured the smallest depth for which the side that is not rate-limited never stalls, for 14 clock ratios (half periods from 1:1 to 2:9 and 9:2 ns): PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME: 0; Equal clocks: depth 4; Ratios such as 3:2, 2:3, 7:5, 5:7: depth 3; Ratios such as 1:2, 2:1, 3:7, 7:3, 9:2: depth 2; Worst case over the 14 ratios: depth 4 PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME: 1; Equal clocks: depth 6; Ratios such as 3:2, 2:3, 7:5, 5:7: depth 4 to 5; Ratios such as 1:2, 2:1, 3:7, 7:3, 9:2: depth 3 to 4; Worst case over the 14 ratios: depth 6 The rule of REQ-PERF-002, depth at least 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME, covers the worst case of the tested ratios.
rules.condition: depth at least 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME, over the tested clock ratios
rules.statement: The side that is not rate-limited never stalls (REQ-PERF-002).

rules.quote: With a smaller depth the FIFO is still correct but a gap appears (for example, equal clocks with depth 3 and PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0).
rules.condition: depth is smaller than needed for gap-free streaming
rules.statement: The FIFO remains functionally correct, although a gap may appear.

rules.quote: The memory is read in every read-clock cycle at the address of the next read pointer.
rules.statement: The memory is read at the address of the next read pointer.

rules.quote: A read of the address that is written at the same edge returns the old word; the flags make this harmless because the read side takes a word only after the flag fell, and the flag falls together with the output register that holds the new word (Section 5.3).
rules.condition: read and write of the same address at the same edge
rules.statement: A read of the address written at the same edge returns the old word, and the read side takes a word only after the flag fell.

rules.quote: The memory is never invalid at an address that is read with o_empty = 0.
rules.statement: The memory must not be invalid at an address that is read.

rules.quote: The pointers and the occupancy are those of Section 9. The occupancy is occ(a, b) = a - b if a is not below b, otherwise a + 2 x DEPTH - b.
rules.statement: Occupancy occ(a,b) = a - b if a is not below b, otherwise a + 2 x DEPTH - b.

rules.quote: Write domain (all flags are flop outputs loaded at the edge, from the next values): Name: block; Definition: o_sw_rst_busy flop OR i_rst_n_sw = 0 Name: rd_ptr_view; Definition: i_rd_ptr if PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0, otherwise the flop that captured i_rd_ptr at the previous edge Name: write accepted; Definition: i_wr_en AND NOT block AND NOT full flop Name: next write pointer; Definition: 0 in state PTR; incremented if a write is accepted; otherwise unchanged Name: next occupancy; Definition: occ(next write pointer, rd_ptr_view) Name: full flop; Definition: next occupancy equals DEPTH Name: full-threshold flop; Definition: next occupancy is at or above i_full_thr
rules.statement: Write-domain flops load at the edge from next values: a write is accepted when i_wr_en, not block and not full flop; the full flop is set when next occupancy equals DEPTH; the full-threshold flop when it reaches i_full_thr.

rules.quote: Name: o_full; Definition: block OR full flop Name: o_full_thr; Definition: if block: (i_full_thr equals 0), otherwise the full-threshold flop
rules.statement: o_full = block OR full flop; o_full_thr = (i_full_thr equals 0) when block, otherwise the full-threshold flop.

rules.quote: Name: o_overflow; Definition: flop: i_wr_en AND NOT block AND full flop, one cycle later
rules.statement: o_overflow is a flop set one cycle after i_wr_en with not block and full flop.

rules.quote: Read domain (all flags are flop outputs loaded at the edge, from the next values): Name: block; Definition: request seen on the read side (directly or through the retiming flop) OR read FSM not in RUN Name: wr_ptr_view; Definition: i_wr_ptr if PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0, otherwise the flop that captured i_wr_ptr at the previous edge Name: read accepted; Definition: i_rd_en AND NOT block AND NOT empty flop Name: next read pointer; Definition: 0 in state RST; incremented if a read is accepted; otherwise unchanged Name: next occupancy; Definition: occ(wr_ptr_view, next read pointer) Name: empty flop; Definition: next occupancy equals 0 Name: empty-threshold flop; Definition: next occupancy is at or below i_empty_thr
rules.statement: Read-domain flops load at the edge from next values: a read is accepted when i_rd_en, not block and not empty flop; the empty flop is set when next occupancy equals 0; the threshold flop when at or below i_empty_thr.

rules.quote: Name: o_empty; Definition: block OR empty flop Name: o_empty_thr; Definition: if block: 1, otherwise the empty-threshold flop
rules.statement: o_empty = block OR empty flop; o_empty_thr = 1 when block, otherwise the empty-threshold flop.

rules.quote: Name: o_underflow; Definition: flop: i_rd_en AND NOT block AND empty flop, one cycle later
rules.statement: o_underflow is a flop set one cycle after i_rd_en with not block and empty flop.

rules.quote: Name: memory read address; Definition: the next read pointer modulo DEPTH
rules.statement: The memory read address is the next read pointer modulo DEPTH.

rules.quote: The write view of the occupancy never underestimates the real occupancy, and the read view never overestimates it, because each view uses a pointer of the other domain that may lag but never leads.
rules.statement: The write view of occupancy never underestimates the real occupancy and the read view never overestimates it.

rules.quote: After reset, o_full_thr is 0 until the first clock edge after release; from then on it follows the formula (even if i_full_thr is 0).
rules.statement: o_full_thr is 0 until the first clock edge after release, then follows the formula even if i_full_thr is 0.

rules.quote: The controller drives i_rst_n_sw to 0 in the write domain. From that cycle writes are blocked (no flop in the path) and o_full is 1.
rules.statement: From that cycle writes are blocked and o_full is 1.

rules.quote: The write FSM leaves RUN, o_sw_rst_busy rises in the next cycle, and the request flop is raised.
rules.statement: The write FSM leaves RUN, o_sw_rst_busy rises in the next cycle, and the request flop is raised.

rules.quote: The read FSM sees the request, blocks reads (o_empty = 1), resets the read pointer (state RST, one cycle) and raises the acknowledge.
rules.statement: The read FSM blocks reads (o_empty = 1), resets the read pointer in state RST for one cycle and raises the acknowledge.

rules.quote: The write FSM sees the acknowledge, resets the write pointer (state PTR, one cycle) and waits in HOLD until i_rst_n_sw is 1.
rules.statement: The write FSM resets the write pointer in state PTR for one cycle and waits in HOLD until i_rst_n_sw is 1.

rules.quote: In REL the request is dropped. The read side leaves ACK first, when it sees the request at 0 and the write pointer at 0 (flush check).
rules.statement: In REL the request is dropped; the read side leaves ACK when it sees the request at 0 and the write pointer at 0.

rules.quote: The write side leaves REL when it sees the acknowledge at 0 and the read pointer at 0, then returns to RUN; o_sw_rst_busy falls.
rules.statement: The write side leaves REL when it sees the acknowledge at 0 and the read pointer at 0, returns to RUN, and o_sw_rst_busy falls.

rules.quote: The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1.
rules.statement: The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1.

rules.quote: A one-cycle low pulse starts the complete sequence.
rules.statement: A one-cycle low pulse on i_rst_n_sw starts the complete software reset sequence.

rules.quote: A hardware reset at any step clears all FSMs.
rules.statement: A hardware reset clears all FSMs.

rules.quote: A new low level during REL is served after the write FSM is back in RUN.
rules.statement: The new low level is served after the write FSM is back in RUN.

rules.quote: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-23): the IP has no software-visible registers; it is configured by parameters (Section 8) and the static threshold inputs.
rules.statement: The IP must not provide software-visible registers; it is configured only by parameters and the static threshold inputs.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-001; Detection condition: Write requested while o_full = 1 and writes are not blocked; Observable response/status: The write is dropped; o_overflow pulses for one cycle; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next request is independent; Reset behavior: Cleared by reset
rules.condition: A write is requested while o_full = 1 and writes are not blocked (ERR-001)
rules.statement: The write must be dropped and o_overflow must pulse for one cycle.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-001; Detection condition: Write requested while o_full = 1 and writes are not blocked; Observable response/status: The write is dropped; o_overflow pulses for one cycle; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next request is independent; Reset behavior: Cleared by reset
rules.statement: The next request must be handled independently of the rejected write, with no recovery action required.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-001; Detection condition: Write requested while o_full = 1 and writes are not blocked; Observable response/status: The write is dropped; o_overflow pulses for one cycle; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next request is independent; Reset behavior: Cleared by reset
rules.statement: The ERR-001 overflow status must be cleared by reset.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-002; Detection condition: Read requested while o_empty = 1 and reads are not blocked; Observable response/status: The read is dropped; o_underflow pulses for one cycle; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next request is independent; Reset behavior: Cleared by reset
rules.condition: A read is requested while o_empty = 1 and reads are not blocked (ERR-002)
rules.statement: The read must be dropped and o_underflow must pulse for one cycle.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-002; Detection condition: Read requested while o_empty = 1 and reads are not blocked; Observable response/status: The read is dropped; o_underflow pulses for one cycle; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next request is independent; Reset behavior: Cleared by reset
rules.statement: The next request must be handled independently of the rejected read, with no recovery action required.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-002; Detection condition: Read requested while o_empty = 1 and reads are not blocked; Observable response/status: The read is dropped; o_underflow pulses for one cycle; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next request is independent; Reset behavior: Cleared by reset
rules.statement: The ERR-002 underflow status must be cleared by reset.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-003; Detection condition: Request while the software reset blocks the side; Observable response/status: The request is dropped; no pulse; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Retry after o_sw_rst_busy = 0; Reset behavior: Not applicable
rules.condition: A request is made while the software reset blocks the side (ERR-003)
rules.statement: The request must be dropped and no overflow or underflow pulse must be generated.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-003; Detection condition: Request while the software reset blocks the side; Observable response/status: The request is dropped; no pulse; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Retry after o_sw_rst_busy = 0; Reset behavior: Not applicable
rules.condition: A request was dropped by software reset blocking
rules.statement: The request may be retried after o_sw_rst_busy = 0.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-004; Detection condition: Illegal parameter value or a threshold changed while in use; Observable response/status: Not detected; behavior not specified; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The integrator fixes the configuration; Reset behavior: Not applicable
rules.condition: Illegal parameter value or threshold changed while in use (ERR-004)
rules.statement: Behavior is not specified and the condition is not detected; no error interrupt is raised and the integrator must fix the configuration.

rules.quote: There is no sticky error and no error interrupt; the pulses are the only status.
rules.statement: There must be no sticky error and no error interrupt; the overflow and underflow pulses are the only error status.

rules.quote: The pulses of consecutive rejected requests are consecutive.
rules.statement: The pulses for consecutive rejected requests must be consecutive, one per rejected request.

rules.quote: There is no data protection (no ECC or parity), so a corrupted stored word is not detected.
rules.statement: There is no ECC or parity data protection, so a corrupted stored word is not detected.

rules.quote: Metric ID: PERF-001; Metric: Throughput; Target / limit: One word per write cycle and one per read cycle; Conditions: Any depth of 2 or more; Measurement method: Simulation: TEST-007; Hard / goal: Hard (REQ-PERF-001)
rules.statement: The FIFO must sustain a throughput of one word per write cycle and one word per read cycle.

rules.quote: Metric ID: PERF-002; Metric: Gap-free streaming; Target / limit: No gap after the initial latency; Conditions: Depth at least 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME; Measurement method: Simulation and depth sweep: TEST-007; Hard / goal: Hard (REQ-PERF-002)
rules.condition: Depth is at least 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME
rules.statement: The FIFO must stream without any gap after the initial latency.

rules.quote: Metric ID: PERF-003; Metric: Write-to-empty-fall latency; Target / limit: First (PTR_RETIME 0) or second (PTR_RETIME 1) read edge strictly after the write edge; Conditions: Any ratio; Measurement method: Simulation: TEST-006; Hard / goal: Hard (REQ-PERF-003)
rules.statement: Empty must fall on the first read edge (PTR_RETIME 0) or second read edge (PTR_RETIME 1) strictly after the write edge.

rules.quote: Metric ID: PERF-004; Metric: Read-to-full-fall latency; Target / limit: First or second write edge strictly after the read edge; Conditions: Any ratio; Measurement method: Simulation: TEST-006; Hard / goal: Hard (REQ-PERF-004)
rules.statement: Full must fall on the first or second write edge strictly after the read edge, depending on PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME.

rules.quote: The VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2 in VLSIT_RTL_Design_Rule.md (REF-003) are the mandatory RTL coding authority. The RTL complies with them without local exceptions.
rules.statement: The RTL must comply with VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2 (REF-003) without local exceptions.

rules.quote: Items that matter most for this IP: one module per file with the file name equal to the module name; a structural top; ANSI ports with input wire and output logic; reg_, w_, p_ff_ and p_com_ names; FSM names reg_fsm_srst_current_state and w_fsm_srst_nxt_state with ENUM_ST_* states and a safe recovery of the unused encodings; parameters PARA_SFIFO_* with the three PAR-02 comment lines; at most 30 characters per name; cell and macro instances named u_dont_touch_ followed by the function name; comment lines of at most 100 characters; port layout and grouping of REF-003 FIL-05 and FIL-06.
rules.statement: The RTL must follow the REF-003 items listed: one module per file, structural top, ANSI ports, naming prefixes, FSM names and ENUM_ST_* states, PARA_SFIFO_* parameters, name and comment length limits, u_dont_touch_ instance names.

rules.quote: Every flop of the control state has an asynchronous reset; the memory is the only resetless storage (DEC-016).
rules.statement: Every flop of the control state must have an asynchronous reset; the memory is the only resetless storage.

rules.quote: No SVA, testbench or prototype code belongs to the synthesis file list.
rules.statement: SVA, testbench or prototype code must not be in the synthesis file list.

rules.quote: The library SRAM and its macro model are in 000_Common, not in the folder of this IP (REQ-RTL-002).
rules.statement: The library SRAM and its macro model must be located in 000_Common, not in the folder of this IP.

rules.quote: Module: m_vlsit_sfifo_top; Responsibility: Structural top: ports, parameters, interconnect, instances; Parent / instance: Top; Clock/reset domains: CLK-WR and CLK-RD; Interface: All ports of Section 6.2 Module: m_vlsit_sfifo_wr; Responsibility: Write side and software reset FSM of the write domain; Parent / instance: m_vlsit_sfifo_top / u_wr; Clock/reset domains: CLK-WR / RST-WR; Interface: Write interface, pointers and handshake, memory write port Module: m_vlsit_sfifo_rd; Responsibility: Read side and software reset FSM of the read domain; Parent / instance: m_vlsit_sfifo_top / u_rd; Clock/reset domains: CLK-RD / RST-RD; Interface: Read interface, pointers and handshake, memory read port Module: m_vlsit_sfifo_mem; Responsibility: Array or SRAM wrapper; Parent / instance: m_vlsit_sfifo_top / u_mem; Clock/reset domains: CLK-WR (write port), CLK-RD (read port); Interface: Memory ports
rules.statement: The hierarchy must have top m_vlsit_sfifo_top with instances u_wr, u_rd and u_mem of modules wr, rd and mem.

rules.quote: Module: m_vlsit_sfifo_ram_macro; Responsibility: SRAM wrapper (library) in 000_Common/rtl_lib; Parent / instance: m_vlsit_sfifo_mem / u_ram_macro (only when PARA_SFIFO_MEM_USE_MACRO = 1); Clock/reset domains: CLK-WR and CLK-RD; Interface: Memory ports with library pin names
rules.statement: m_vlsit_sfifo_ram_macro is instantiated as u_ram_macro in m_vlsit_sfifo_mem only when PARA_SFIFO_MEM_USE_MACRO = 1.

rules.quote: State is owned by wr (write pointer, write flags, write FSM, retiming flops of the read pointer and acknowledge), by rd (read pointer, read flags, read FSM, retiming flops of the write pointer and request) and by mem (storage).
rules.statement: State ownership: wr owns write pointer, flags, FSM and read-pointer/ack retiming flops; rd owns read-side equivalents; mem owns storage.

rules.quote: There is no register logic and no protocol adapter.
rules.statement: The design must have no register logic and no protocol adapter.

rules.statement: o_mem_wr_data is a copy of i_wr_data in the same cycle.

rules.statement: o_req_wr is a flop output, reset to 0, set with the busy flop and cleared when REL starts.

rules.statement: o_rd_ptr is a flop output that changes only at the read-clock edge that accepts a read, and resets to 0.

Term / acronym: Synchronous clocks; Definition: Two clocks derived from one source with a fixed phase relationship, possibly of different frequency
Term / acronym: Timed path; Definition: A path between flops of two related clocks that STA closes at the nearest launch and capture edges
Term / acronym: Occupancy; Definition: Number of words stored: write pointer minus read pointer, modulo two times the depth
Term / acronym: View; Definition: The occupancy as seen by one side, using the pointer of the other side that may lag
Term / acronym: Show-ahead; Definition: The read data already shows the word at the read pointer before the read request
Term / acronym: Look-ahead flag; Definition: A flag flop loaded from the next pointer values
Term / acronym: Gap-free streaming; Definition: After the initial latency, one word accepted in every clock cycle of the side that is not limited by the clock ratio
Term / acronym: PTR_RETIME; Definition: The parameter that adds one retiming flop to the pointers and handshake signals that cross to another domain
Term / acronym: Block term; Definition: Software reset block of a side: busy flop or i_rst_n_sw low (write), request seen or FSM not in RUN (read)
Term / acronym: FSM; Definition: Finite-state machine
Term / acronym: SRAM macro; Definition: A library memory with one write port and one read port behind a wrapper
